newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs seen crumbling to 127.72.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs seen crumbling to 127.72.

text.p: June BTP futures on LIFFE may slip through a series of support levels and possibly hit a one-month low of 127.72, technical analysts said on Monday.
BTPs were hammered at the opening in line with sliding French bonds after a left-wing victory in Sunday's French election. By 0755 GMT, the June BTP contract traded 40 basis points lower at 128.50.

Anne Whitby, head of technical analysis at 4CAST in London, said support was likely to fail at 128.06 -- the low on Friday -- and also at 128.03, which is around a 61.8 percent retracement of the rally from 125.80 on April 25 to 131.40 on May 21.

"There will be a bit of support at 128.06 but I would expect it to break down after that," said Whitby. If the area between 127.72 and 127.63 was also taken out, BTPs would risk surrendering to the April 30 low of 127.14, she said.
"But I don't think we'll get there today," said Whitby, although 127.72 was "quite likely" to be seen on Monday.
On the upside, Monday's high of 128.75 was first resistance but gains above the heavy congestion area of 129.00, which is also Friday's high, were unlikely.
"You have to see it breaking through that to turn round," said Whitby.
An analyst at an Italian bank in London agreed.
"Technical indicators and oscillators are all in sell. There is no signal for a rally at the moment," he said.
Below Friday's low of 128.06, the market risked triggering sell stops, speeding up the losses to 127.75. This level appeared a strong support on 60-minute charts, he said.
"I don't see the market below this level," he said, adding that the lira's recovery against the mark on Monday should also prove supportive for BTPs.
By 0830 GMT, the June Eurolira future stood seven basis points lower at 93.07.
